M2.reason: Measured length is 18.9 against the 18 asked (offset 0.047), within 15%. The first-person measure of 19.1 is also within range.

M3.reason: The handle and head are present. The toothed jaw is only a few small bumps on one end of the head in the left view, and no moving jaw or adjusting nut appears in any view. The brief's jaw is missing its key parts.

M4.reason: The handle is red with grey bands where the paint is worn to bare iron, as the brief asks. The head is grey steel with rust stains. The colours and materials match the brief's words.

M5.reason: Rust patches and worn bands are present and sharp enough at this scale. The head's speckled texture reads a little like concrete, and the teeth have no visible detail, so the surface detail is only partly there.

M6.reason: In the line-up, the wrench (D) is clearly a different kind of object from the game's items. Beside Half-Life's own weapons, though, it reads as a hammer or sledge rather than a wrench, so a player would not take it for one of the game's.

M7.reason: The brief sets no front. The front view shows the handle end facing the viewer, and the picture does not establish an upright front or where the origin sits. The check cannot be settled from these pictures.

M8.reason: The measured checks report no errors. The model has 104 triangles, well under twice any reasonable median for a Half-Life weapon. The views show the handle meeting the head with no visible gaps or floating parts.
